_doc: This is a collection of 16 independent Scala learning exercises, not an application.
There is no repo-root build: 3 of the 16 directories have a build.sbt, the other 13 are
IntelliJ/Eclipse modules with no build tool at all. Every command/health-check field is
therefore null or empty, and the per-project commands that DO work are recorded in gotchas
so a role can run them explicitly instead of guessing at a repo-wide one.
estate_role: Standalone. A personal Scala/Akka workshop repository of self-contained exercises; it has no siblings, publishes no artifact and is consumed by nothing, so there is no cross-repo merge order to derive.
stack: Scala 2.12 in the three sbt projects (2.12.2 in actors and actorssimple, 2.12.4 in actors-heirarchy) with Akka 2.5.3 (akka-actor, akka-testkit, akka-remote) and ScalaTest 3.0.1. Builds are sbt where they exist (0.13.16 in actors and actorssimple, 1.1.0 in actors-heirarchy); the remaining 13 exercise directories are IntelliJ .iml / Eclipse .classpath modules with no build definition. Those IDE modules mostly declare scala-sdk-2.12.4, with two exceptions that matter: Assignment11 also lists an application-level scala-sdk-2.10.4 (Assignment10 lists only 2.12.4, though both bundle Scala 2.10 test jars — see gotchas), and ActorHeir is an Eclipse project declaring scala-sdk-2.11.11 with its .classpath pointing at Akka 2.3.15 jars under absolute Windows paths (F:/Tools/...) that exist on nobody's machine. The sbt builds require JDK 8 — they do not run on the JDK 17 that is the runner default.
conventions: One exercise per top-level directory, each fully self-contained. Projects never import from one another, and duplicated model classes across directories are intentional — see review_checklist.
The three sbt projects use standard Maven layout (src/main/scala/...); the IDE-only modules use a flat src/ (plus test/ in Assignment10 and Assignment11) with the package path beneath it.

Packages are com.scala.<topic> (com.scala.futures, com.scala.currying, com.scala.assignment9), com.scalalab.<layer> (Assignment10, Assignment11) or com.sample.actor.<layer> (ActorHeir, actors-heirarchy), with sub-packages named for the role they hold: model, reader, worker/workers, sender, receiver, printer, starter, root.

Runnable entry points are a bare `object`, never a class, and both JVM idioms are in use: 12 objects `extend App` with the work in the object body (MessagingSystem, FuturesExample, FuturesAndPromises, FutureWithMap, Boot in both ActorHeir and actors-heirarchy, Main in `Assignment 10`, Assignment9, RemoteActorSystem, System, PingPongSystem, ImplicitExample), and 7 declare `def main(args: Array[String]): Unit` instead (Assignment1, Assignment2, Assignment3, Assignment4, Currying, and Starter in both Assignment10 and Assignment11). Follow whichever the directory you are editing already uses.

Domain types are case classes with a companion object that both holds the in-memory state (a mutable ListBuffer seeded with sample rows) and exposes the operations over it — see Assignment10/src/com/scalalab/model/Event.scala.

Absence is modelled with Option and consumed by pattern matching (`case Some(e) => ... case None => ...`), never by returning null. Error cases throw a purpose-named Exception subclass declared on the method with @throws — EventNotAvailableException is the pattern.

Shared behaviour is mixed in as a trait rather than inherited from a class (`object Event extends StringConverter`), and implicit conversions live in a trait that the user mixes in (Implicits/src/com/scala/implicits/StringConverter.scala).
Asynchronous work uses scala.concurrent.Future with `import scala.concurrent.ExecutionContext.Implicits.global` at the use site, and results are consumed with onComplete/andThen over Success/Failure.

Akka actors are created through a companion `props` (actors) or directly with `Props[T]` from a parent's context (actors-heirarchy, ActorHeir, actorssimple), and state changes go through context.become.
review_checklist: Confirm the change stays inside the one exercise directory it targets. Assignment10 and Assignment11 are deliberate near-duplicate variants of the same exercise, ActorHeir/src and actors-heirarchy/src/main/scala are byte-identical copies of each other, and Event/Device/StringConverter exist in four separate copies on purpose — extracting a shared module destroys the point of the exercises. Reject 'deduplication' refactors unless the issue explicitly asked for one.

There is no .gitignore, and build output is tracked in git (160 files under */target, plus .class and .jar). Check the diff contains no regenerated build artifacts, no .idea/ churn, and no .cache/.classpath noise — compiling all three sbt projects dirties ~150 tracked files that must be restored before committing.

If the change touches actors, actorssimple or actors-heirarchy, any newly imported library needs a matching libraryDependencies entry in that project's build.sbt. actors-heirarchy is the standing counter-example: it imports Akka and declares nothing, so it does not compile.

If the change touches any of the other 13 directories, no build tool compiles it — nothing in CI will catch a syntax error. Say so in the review rather than treating an absent failure as a pass. The two EventSpec suites are the one exception: they can be compiled and run by hand (see qa_notes).

Keep to Scala 2.12 and Akka 2.5 era APIs in the sbt projects. Scala 2.13+ collection methods or Akka 2.6+ (typed actors, ActorSystem[T]) will not compile against the pinned versions. Assignment10 and Assignment11 are the reverse case — their bundled test jars are Scala 2.10, so their test sources must stay inside what 2.10 accepts.
Directory names are load-bearing and awkward: `Assignment 10` (with a space) is a different exercise from `Assignment10`. Check paths in the diff are the intended ones and are quoted in any script.
qa_notes: The repository has exactly two test files: Assignment10/test/com/scalalab/model/EventSpec.scala and Assignment11/test/com/scalalab/model/EventSpec.scala. They are ScalaTest FlatSpec with Matchers, using the `"subject" should "behaviour" in { ... }` string form, and they assert against the companion-object in-memory state (Event.findAllEvents, Event.addEvent, Event.updateEvent).

Both suites work — 4 tests each, 8 in total, all passing — but only under Scala 2.10, which is what their bundled lib/ jars are built for. There is no build definition to run them, so it is a hand-rolled compile: with JDK 8, compile <module>/src then <module>/test with scala-compiler-2.10.6 and `<module>/lib/scalatest_2.10-3.0.1.jar:<module>/lib/scalactic_2.10-3.0.1.jar` on the classpath, then run org.scalatest.tools.Runner -R <test-classes-dir>. Compiling the same test sources with Scala 2.12 fails — see gotchas.

actors, actorssimple and actors-heirarchy declare scalatest and akka-testkit in build.sbt but contain no src/test sources at all. `sbt test` in actors succeeds having run 0 tests, so a green sbt test is not evidence of anything — check the reported test count.

Nothing is mocked anywhere and there are no fixtures; state comes from hard-coded sample data in companion objects and in HardCodedEventDataReader. Follow that when adding tests rather than introducing a mocking framework.

Tests share mutable global state: Event.events is a ListBuffer on the companion object that addEvent and updateEvent mutate, so the existing specs are order-dependent (one asserts the list size is exactly 5 after an insert). Adding a test that touches Event will change what the existing ones see.
gotchas: There is no repo-root build file and no repo-wide test/build/lint command — that is why commands.test, commands.build and commands.lint are all null. Do not invent a root-level `sbt` invocation: run at a project directory, and only for the three that have a build.sbt.

PRE-EXISTING FAILURE: actors-heirarchy does not compile on a clean checkout. Its build.sbt declares zero libraryDependencies while its sources import akka.actor.Actor/Props/ActorSystem/OneForOneStrategy and akka.util.Timeout, giving 38 'not found: value Props / not found: type Receive / not found: value context' errors. Re-verified under JDK 8 with its pinned sbt 1.1.0. Do not attribute this to your delta, and do not 'fix' it as a drive-by — it is a separate issue. ActorHeir holds a byte-identical copy of the same sources and has no build tool at all, so it does not compile either.

The Assignment10/Assignment11 test jars are Scala 2.10 (scalatest_2.10-3.0.1.jar, scalactic_2.10-3.0.1.jar), not 2.12. Compiling those test sources with the scala-sdk-2.12.4 the .iml files list fails with 'value should is not a member of String' and 'can't expand macros compiled by previous versions of Scala' (23 errors in Assignment10). Under Scala 2.10.6 the same sources compile and all 4 tests pass in each module. The main sources of both modules compile under either version. So this is a toolchain mismatch to work around, not a broken test suite — do not 'fix' the specs.

The runner has no sbt and no scala/scalac installed; only java (JDK 8, 11, 17, 21 and 25 under /usr/lib/jvm, with JAVA_HOME defaulting to 17), maven, gradle and node. An sbt launcher has to be fetched before any build command will run.

The pinned sbt versions do not work on the default JDK. sbt 0.13.16 (actors, actorssimple) and 1.1.0 (actors-heirarchy) both die on JDK 17 with 'java.io.IOError: java.lang.RuntimeException: /packages cannot be represented as URI'. Set JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/temurin-8-jdk-amd64 to build.

VERIFIED WORKING: with JAVA_HOME set to temurin-8 and an sbt launcher on PATH, `cd actors && sbt compile` and `cd actorssimple && sbt compile` both succeed (7 and 9 Scala sources, one feature warning each). `cd actors && sbt test` succeeds but runs 0 tests.

Running any sbt command mutates files that are tracked in git: build output under */target is committed to the repository, so compiling all three sbt projects leaves ~150 modified and deleted tracked files (149 measured). Always `git checkout -- . && git clean -fd` after building and before staging, or the build artifacts land in the PR.

`Assignment 10` (with a space) and `Assignment10` are two different exercises with different packages — com.scala.assignment10 and com.scalalab respectively. Quote paths in every shell command that touches them.

Assignment10 and Assignment11 are near-identical by design; only Event.scala, Starter.scala and EventSpec.scala differ between them (plus .iml/.idea metadata). A change intended for one must not be mirrored into the other unless the issue says so.
openspec/ currently contains only config.yaml — there are no existing changes or specs to read for precedent.
reuse_hotspots: Assignment10/src/com/scalalab/model/ and Assignment11/src/com/scalalab/model/ — Event, Device, StringConverter, EventNotAvailableException. The most-copied types in the repo; check here first for an existing shape to follow, but copy rather than share (see review_checklist).
actors/src/main/scala/com/scala/actors/model/ — the same Event, Device, StringConverter and EventNotAvailableException in their Akka form.
`Assignment 10`/src/com/scala/assignment10/reader/ — DataReader[T] plus its hard-coded implementation, the repo's only abstraction-over-a-source pattern.
Assignment9/src/com/scala/assignment9/ — OutputWriter trait and GenericObjectWriter, the repo's generic/higher-order-function helpers.
Implicits/src/com/scala/implicits/ — the reference implementation for implicit conversions in a trait.

notes: Nothing here is deployed. There is no staging branch, no container, no service and no published artifact — the repository is exercise source read by a human in an IDE.

There is no CI that builds this code: the only workflows are .github/workflows/factory-pipeline.yml and factory-branch-guard.yml, neither of which compiles Scala. A merge is therefore never validated by a build unless a role ran one by hand and said so.
Consequently there is no release train to halt and no post-merge verification to run. A release role should treat a merged PR here as complete.
